scenes.headline: How DeepInfer moves a request through prefill and decode
scenes.sub: The engine behind DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, now open source
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Orrery! Here is how DeepInfer, DeepSeek's newly opened engine, serves one request.

scenes.text: DeepSeek released the engine that runs prefill and decode. The store, the transfer and the balancers around it are described, not shipped.
scenes.say: The release is the engine. The storage, the transfer and the balancers are described, but kept back.

scenes.title: The system it was cut from

steps.say: A request enters through the recipe, which makes tokens, and the entrypoint, which routes it.
Prefill and decode are separate services, each behind its own balancer, over a shared cache store.
The recipe encodes the request. The entrypoint matches its prefix against the store.
A prefill engine swaps the cached part in, and computes only the new tokens.
The cache and window state move to a decode engine on sixty four GPUs or more.
Decode streams tokens out, and writes its cache back.

scenes.title: Bounded replay after a cache hit

steps.label: Sliding window
steps.say: Many layers look back over a short sliding window.

steps.label: Replay the tail
steps.say: After a cache hit, DeepInfer recomputes just the last hundred and twenty eight tokens. It is approximate.

scenes.title: How many drafts to verify
scenes.say: Decode uses DSpark. The trick is choosing how much to verify.

items.say: A confidence head rates each draft's chance to survive.

items.text: Sort every draft in the batch
items.say: Every draft in the batch is sorted by that chance.

items.text: Grow the step while it pays
items.say: The scheduler adds them until tokens per millisecond stop rising.

scenes.title: What the decode chart multiplies by

parts.say: The headline chart measures steps per second, times tau.
Tau assumes three drafts, each accepted three quarters of the time.
DeepSeek's own numbers suggest that is high by about a sixth.

scenes.title: Per decode GPU, near the same per-user speed
scenes.say: On one denominator, at matched speed, DeepInfer's chart is about one and a half times the best vLLM run.

scenes.text: The engine is open. The service around it, and a like-for-like benchmark, are not yet.

recap: C++ scheduler, TileLang glue, DeepSeek kernels
Verify drafts while the step still pays
The headline chart assumes an acceptance
scenes.say: An open engine, a greedy verifier, and a chart to read closely.
